Specimen ontology rules, version 2.0. Each rule names its Darwin Core term and how it is checked.
- one_collecting_event: A specimen has one collecting event. When two of its labels write two different collecting dates, or two place names (letter case, accents, punctuation and unit words such as "Dept." aside) that no source the answer cites confirms as one place, an answer that settles the field on one label's text is refused. (Darwin Core: Event: eventDate; dcterms:Location: locality; checked by code.)
- place_within_settled_places: The apply-time refusal stays as today: it checks a candidate against the settled country and province, but a city against a settled county only for a near spelling. On the units path the check stage marks for a person a place below the country, settled on a source record that names its parents, whose record and the settled country's record name two different nations by an identity both carry: the record's country (its last parent) and the settled country carry different ISO 3166-1 codes, or both are Getty TGN records and the place's chain ends at another TGN nation's record the stage knows to be a nation. The country Georgia settled on Wikidata's nation (GE), a county Fulton on NGA's record in the US state Georgia (US), is marked. Below the country it marks nothing: a place is inside a settled province when that province's record is among its record's parents, and otherwise the check abstains. A person's value is never marked. (Darwin Core: country, stateProvince, county, municipality; checked by code.)
- place_chain: The places form one chain, country > province or state > county > city. On the units path the check stage marks for a person a place settled on a source record whose record and a place settled above it name two different nations by an identity both carry (the test of the rule place_within_settled_places); a derived country is marked by the rule place_parents_derived. Below the country a place is in the chain when the settled place's record is among its record's parents, and otherwise the check abstains: a settled Coles County, then an exact "Chicago" whose TGN preferred chain is Cook County, Illinois and the United States, is not marked, and is marked only when the record's whole parent set is known. A place an earlier attempt settled is checked on its record read again from the record's own stored responses. A person's value is never marked. (Darwin Core: country, stateProvince, county, municipality; checked by code.)
- date_order: The collecting date is on or before the determination date; the same day is allowed. Dates written at different precisions compare on the parts both have ("1946" and "1946-09-06" agree). On the units path a settled determination dated before the settled collecting date is marked for a person by the check stage, both dates listed, and the run's date_order reason compares the two dates the same way. (Darwin Core: eventDate, dateIdentified; checked by code.)
- day_month_order: A numeric date whose two orders, day-month and month-day, give two different dates is never settled on either reading by the date check. (Darwin Core: eventDate, dateIdentified; checked by code.)
- code_is_no_date: Codes are never dates nor any part of them: a slide code such as "IV-29-68-4" beside the collecting date "IV-23-48" is no date. On the units path the date check gives no date for a literal that any reading writes inside a slide code, a match of the file's slide-code forms that holds the literal, even where that reading glues a letter to it: the literal "I-23-48", reading A "Guatemala I-23-48", reading B "Guatemala VI-23-48-4". A date that punctuation separates from a code beside it ("IV-23-48;IV-29-68-4") is still a date. Each occurrence of the literal in each reading counts: one inside a code makes it no date. (Darwin Core: ours: no Darwin Core term fits a code; eventDate; checked by code.)
- label_type_routing: A label's type (locality, determination, code) and a unit's fields, the file's routing advice, name the experts a unit is for and never keep a field's expert from a unit: every expert's request carries every label's readings whole and, on the units path, every unit with its fields, so a determination label that writes a locality reaches the locality expert. (Darwin Core: ours: no Darwin Core term fits a label; checked by code.)
- elevation_unit_feet: An elevation whose cleared text writes no unit is read as feet only when (a) at least one reader wrote the foot mark or "ft" at this unit, (b) the number read as metres is above the highest point of the specimen's country, which is cleared, not marked (the highest-point table), and (c) the number read as feet is possible (16000 with a mark is not, in the Philippines). When all hold, the elevation settles in feet, cleared, its reason "Basis: inferred, rule elevation_unit_feet". Without (a) the field is unresolved: magnitude alone never decides; so it is when (b) or (c) fails or the country is marked. Terrain takes no part while the owner's decision D5 is held. (Darwin Core: verbatimElevation, minimumElevationInMeters, maximumElevationInMeters; checked by code.)
- elevation_needs_a_unit: An answer that settles an elevation field on a number that one of its readings writes with no unit anywhere in that reading is refused: a unit is never guessed from the magnitude, the place or a map. (Darwin Core: verbatimElevation, minimumElevationInMeters, maximumElevationInMeters; checked by code.)
- elevation_unit_decides_field: An answer that settles an elevation field on a number that one of its readings writes in the other unit is refused. (Darwin Core: verbatimElevation, minimumElevationInMeters, maximumElevationInMeters; checked by code.)
- place_parents_derived: Upward derivation (a country from a settled province) stays as today and fills only open fields; a province derived from a county is the county's province-level parent, the first of the two or more its record names, never the country. The place chains that derivation fills are checked against the place chain on the units path: a derived country is marked for a person when a place settled below it, on a source record that names its parents, names another nation by an identity both carry (the test of the rule place_within_settled_places), unless a person kept it, when the place below it is marked instead. A derived province or county is never marked: below the country the check abstains. A province "Cook" unresolved, a settled county Cook in Illinois and a settled city Gary in Indiana: the province is derived as Illinois, and is not marked on TGN's preferred chain alone. (Darwin Core: country, stateProvince, county; checked by code.)
- elevation_conversion: A derived elevation is a stated one copied to the other end of its unit, or its exact conversion (1 ft = 0.3048 m) rounded to the hundredth; a derived elevation never replaces a stated one; and no elevation is derived while an elevation field is neither settled nor open (one the readings disagree on goes to a person first). On the units path an elevation field is never settled absent while another elevation field is ambiguous, unresolved or unknown: it waits, unknown, its reason naming that field, and is derived once that field settles. (Darwin Core: verbatimElevation, minimumElevationInMeters, maximumElevationInMeters; checked by code.)
- end_date_from_one_date: A derived Date Visited To is the date of a settled Date Visited From, at its precision, and is never derived from a written range. On the units path Date Visited To is never settled absent while Date Visited From is ambiguous, unresolved or unknown: it waits, unknown, its reason naming Date Visited From, and is derived once that date settles. (Darwin Core: eventDate; checked by code.)
- precise_location_extent: Precise Location is the label's locality as written: every line of its locality text, with its line breaks, the higher places and an elevation written among those lines included. It is never cut to the first line, and a label whose locality names nothing finer than its town, or than its country, still has a Precise Location: those lines as written. On the units path a precise location that names nothing finer than its town is never cleared as not on the label; one that holds an elevation settles only when its elevation text is the literal an elevation field settled from that label; and one whose literal, wherever a reading of its label writes it, ends its line before a line that writes the settled province's or country's text is marked for a person as cut short. (Darwin Core: verbatimLocality; checked by code.)

Not rules:
- taxon_regional_occurrence: A taxon's regional occurrence is not a rule: that an authority records no occurrence of a taxon in a region does not make it impossible there, and no check uses occurrence while the owner's decision D4 is held. (Darwin Core: scientificName; dcterms:Location.)
